newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow after slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow after slow trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended lower for the first time in five sessions Tuesday on a lack of interest from foreign investors.
"The Dow recovered towards the close and that promptly revived a few stocks," said Gerardo Copca, associate director of research at the Finamex brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 8.61 points, or 0.23 percent, at 3,784.22.
Trading volume was dull at 42.7 million shares.

"The market, however, is still awaiting developments in U.S. interest rates and (first quarter) domestic corporate earnings. Volume is slow as brokers are switching stocks, and there are no foreign investors in the market," Copca added.

A Reuters survey of money market dealers showed they were expecting Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury bill) rates at 22.66 percent at its weekly auction later in the day -- a rise of 0.80 percentage point since the previous auction.
Traders noted that Alfa, Grupo Carso and Cemex all staged late recoveries that helped the IPC to rebound from a low of 3,764.63 points.

Industrial conglomerate Alfa A shares climbed 1.25 pesos (16 centavos) at 45.25 pesos ($5.72), cement makers Cemex CPO gained 35 centavos (4 cents) to 29.00 pesos ($3.67) while holding company Grupo Carso edged up 15 centavos (2 cents) to 46.45 pesos ($5.85).

Telecommunications firm Telmex, down 18 centavos (2 cents) to 15.78 pesos ($2.00), and financial group GFB, which declined three centavos (less than 1 cent) to 2.77 pesos (35 cents), weighed most on the downside, traders said.
The broad market scoreboard shadowed performance by blue chips, with decliners outnumbering gainers by 51 to 28.
